content.title: OSHA Basics – Workplace Safety 101 From SafetyVideos.com
content.text: Want a COMPLETE training kit including video, employee quiz, answer sheet, and Training Completion Certificate? Complete training kit (without PREVIEW on video) can be purchased here: https://www.safetyvideos.com/Intro_to... This video serves as an introduction to OSHA (Occupational Safety and Health Administration), explaining its origins, mission, and the rights and responsibilities it enforces for both employees and employers. It highlights how OSHA plays a crucial role in ensuring safe and healthy workplaces across various industries. Key points covered OSHA's purpose and creation Established in 1970 under the Occupational Safety and Health Act to safeguard workers' health and safety. Rights of workers Right to a safe workplace Protection from hazards with proper training and equipment. Right to know about hazardous substances Employers must provide safety data sheets and training on chemical hazards. Right to file complaints and participate in inspections Employees can report unsafe conditions without fear of retaliation. Employer responsibilities Comply with OSHA standards, including the General Duty Clause. Provide training, implement safety measures, and supply appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE). Maintain records of workplace injuries and illnesses and report serious incidents promptly. OSHA inspections Include stages like the opening conference, workplace walkaround, and closing conference. Prioritize imminent danger situations, complaints, and fatal incidents. Resources for safety OSHA’s website, workplace safety materials, and external sources like libraries and healthcare professionals. By understanding OSHA’s role and actively participating in workplace safety, both employees and employers contribute to a safer and healthier work environment.
